ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure shows the distribution of local isobars in Europe, with the unit being hPa. In northwestern Europe, near Iceland, a low-pressure center can be seen; near the center it is labeled at about 996 hPa, and the surrounding isobars are roughly 1004, 1008, 1012, 1016 hPa, etc., with air pressure increasing from the center outward; near eastern Europe there is a closed high-pressure area, labeled at about 1024 hPa. Then reason: An obvious Icelandic low and a relatively strong high pressure in eastern Europe or the European continent are relatively common pressure situations in the winter half-year; in summer, the European continent is heated, and it is usually not easy to form such an obvious cold high pressure, and the Icelandic low is also relatively weaker. Therefore, the time shown in this figure is least likely to be in summer.
